messages:
devon: paging alert just fired for continuous-batcher on us-west-2-gpupool-3. queue depth steadily increasing > 1200, a bunch of pods OOMKilled; seeing repeated CUDA allocation failures. paging started ~ 21:10 UTC.
oncall-bot: INCIDENT PAGER — Severity: P2 — continuous-batcher high queue growth (auto-notify) :rotating_light:
 - Alert: batcher_queue_length > 800 for 5m
 - Suspected impacts: latency spikes, 5xx for streaming customers

maria: looking. can you paste a pod name and `kubectl describe` output?
devon: pod: cbatch-7f8b9-0 on node gpu-24. logs show repeated OOM then restart loop. snippet:
```
2026-03-15T21:09:58Z ERROR runtime::alloc - CUDA failed to allocate 3.2G: out of memory
2026-03-15T21:10:01Z WARN batcher - queue_size=985 inflight=12 avg_latency=342ms
2026-03-15T21:10:06Z ERROR containerd: oom killed process 1 (continuous-batcher)
```

oncall-bot: @maria assigned. escalation to eng-runtime oncall.

maria: ok starting triage. first thought: continuous-batcher batch-growth + KV cache retention causing unexpected mem amplification when many small prompts join.

alex: I'm on infra side — node gpu-24 is flapping, kernel logs show PCI reset events before container restarts. might be correlated.
samir: if node is flapping, best immediate step is cordon and drain to avoid more customer impact. preparing drain now.
devon: customer impact: multiple streaming requests for large-gen customers saw 5xx or hang. Support ticket 46231 flagged. Caroline, can you confirm scope?
caroline: confirmed — 3 customers reported errors in last 20m, highest impact for tenant: big-retailer-prod (steady streams). They're seeing partial responses and reconnect churn. Notified them.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0315-07 — continuous-batcher node-flap + OOM. Severity: P2. Channels: eng-runtime, eng-oncall, support.

maria: mitigation plan: 1) disable large-batch composition on batcher (feature flag) 2) drain node gpu-24 3) scale up batcher-worker replicas with smaller instance class to absorb traffic. Doing 1 now.
devon: how do we toggle the flag?
maria: `POST /config/flags/continuous_batching` payload `{ "max_batch_tokens": 1024, "enable_composition": false }` — applying. (reaction: :white_check_mark:)

samir: `kubectl cordon gpu-24 && kubectl drain gpu-24 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force` — starting drain. moving 6 pods off.

alex: watch for eviction-induced transient OOMs; we'll put batcher pods on nodes with larger memory instead of same pool.

21:12 UTC
maria: flag applied. sending patch to config service... confirmed config propagated to 98% of batchers. avg queue size dropped from 980 -> 240 in ~90s.
devon: logs now show less KV growth but still seeing a couple CUDA errs on restarts.

samir: drain completed, node cordoned. re-scheduling to gpu-32/gpu-34.

21:15 UTC
caroline: customers reporting decreased errors, big-retailer-prod still had a single reconnect but no data loss.
tim: pinging account team and CS to set expectations — will update them on postmortem.

maria: follow-up actions to stop recurrence:
- add a hard cap at batcher level `max_total_tokens` to prevent runaway composition (config + codeguard)
- add early OOM detector in runtime to fail-fast and fallback to small-batch sync path
- add node-level PCI reset monitoring and automated node retirement if >3 resets in 10m
- add an alert for sustained queue growth even with composition disabled

devon: agree. also we should backfill the eviction policy to avoid pushing all pods to same target nodes during drain — that's contributing to momentary memory pressure.

alex: quick kube commands I ran:
```
# cordon + drain
kubectl cordon gpu-24
kubectl drain gpu-24 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force
# scale new replicas on larger flavor
kubectl -n infra scale deployment/continuous-batcher --replicas=18
```

21:22 UTC
caroline: support update: ETA to customers said 30m for full stabilization. they're ok for now.

maria: tagging this for a full incident review. assigning owners: maria (runtime fixes), samir (node retirement + infra alerts), devon (postmortem write-up), caroline & tim (customer comms).

oncall-bot: handoff reminder — if this is still active at 22:00 UTC escalate to oncall lead.

21:25 UTC
later note from devon: queue normalized to ~50, no further OOMs in 10m. marking incident as mitigated but not resolved. will open follow-up JIRA for code changes.

21:27 UTC
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — mitigated state. Actions: drain completed, flag disabled, scale up done. Next: postmortem and infra tickets.

21:29 UTC
maria: posting a short repro: when continuous composition receives > 600 small requests/sec and median prompt length < 16 tokens, it can create combined batches with effective token count > 6k due to KV reuse bug. repro attached to Jira INFR-2329.

21:31 UTC
samir: infra task created: INFRA-4032 (node reset detector + auto-retire).

21:34 UTC
devon: closing timeline for now. will reopen if we see regressions. thanks everyone for quick triage. :heart:
